newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians protest settlement with crucifixion.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians protest settlement with crucifixion.

text.p: Palestinians staged a mock crucifixion on Wednesday to protest against Israeli construction of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.

About 50 Palestinians planted three huge wooden crosses opposite Jabal Abu Ghneim, a hill of pine trees where Israeli bulldozers on Tuesday broke ground to construct 6,500 homes for Jews. Israel calls the site Har Homa.
Protesters tied one Palestinian, wearing a crown of thorns, to a cross and hung a sign around his neck bearing the word 'Jerusalem'.
"This activity is symbolic. It has no religious meaning," said Jad Ishaq, an organiser of the protest.
"What we are doing is to send a message to all peace-loving people expressing our willingness to live in peace with each other," he said.

Palestinians view the project as an attempt to cut off East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967, from its West Bank hinterland. Israel views all of Jerusalem as its eternal capital. Palestinians regard the city's Arab East as capital of a future state.
